tip: Jag vill ha en öl is blunt for ordering. Kan jag få en öl is politer when you ask for something.

target: Jag borde ringa henne efter jobbet här.
english: I should call her after work here.
tip: "Borde" = should/ought to. It implies advice or mild obligation.

target: Det visar sig att de inte visste.
english: It turns out that they didn't know.
tip: In att-clauses inte comes before the verb: att de inte visste = that they didn't know.

target: Kan jag betala med kort under sommaren?
english: Can I pay by card during the summer?
tip: Sweden is nearly cashless, so betala med kort works almost everywhere and cash is often refused.

target: Får jag sitta här på kvällen redan?
english: May I sit here in the evening already?
tip: "Får jag" = may I. Polite but not overly formal.

english: We are meeting at five o'clock.
tip: "Ska" for plans/arrangements: "Vi ska träffas" = we're meeting (arranged).

target: Det vill säga, vi har två alternativ.
english: That is to say, we have two options.
tip: "Det vill säga" (dvs.) = that is (i.e.).

target: Hej då och tack för en fantastisk kväll med er.
english: Goodbye and thank you for a fantastic evening with you.
tip: 'Med' (with) – companionship or means: 'med familjen' (with family), 'med tåg' (by train).

target: Får jag presentera min kollega som jobbar på samma kontor?
english: May I introduce my colleague who works at the same office?
tip: 'Få' (may/get to) – dual meaning: 'Du får gå' (You may go) or 'Jag får en present' (I get a gift).
Henne is the object form of hon. Subject is hon, but after a verb it becomes henne: De överraskade henne = they surprised her.
Förlät is the past of the strong verb förlåta (forgive). The vowel shifts, förlåta becomes förlät, with no -de ending.
The -s on opereras makes it passive: not he operates, but he must be operated on. Adding -s to the verb is a common way to form the passive.
Lyssna needs på for what you listen to: lyssnade på honom = listened to him. You cannot say lyssna honom.
To use the adjective fri (free) as an adverb, add the neuter -tt: välja fritt = choose freely.
Bättre is the irregular comparative of bra (good) and väl (well). There is no bra-are; it just becomes bättre.
"Inte" goes after the verb in main clauses: subject + verb + inte.
Får here means be allowed to, not get: jag får vara med = I am allowed to join.
Lägga sig, literally lay oneself, means go to bed: de lägger sig = they go to bed. The reflexive sig is required.

english: The dog is in the park.
tip: Swedish adds the as a suffix, not a separate word: hund becomes hunden (the dog) and park becomes parken (the park).

english: We should see each other more often.
tip: The -s on ses gives a reciprocal meaning, each other: vi borde ses = we should see each other.
Bestämma sig means make up your mind; plain bestämma means decide something. Here mig marks the reflexive: bestämma mig.
Ska inte here means shouldn't, more an instruction than the future: du ska inte vara orolig = you shouldn't worry.
Det här means this, written as two words: det plus här. Vi kan lösa det här = we can solve this.
Ge upp means give up. The particle upp carries the stress and turns ge (give) into give up.

english: It's not as cold as before.
tip: Lika means as in comparisons: inte lika kallt = not as cold. The full frame is lika ... som (as ... as).
Bil is an en-word, so the adjective stays röd. An ett-word would take rött, as in ett rött hus.
After tillåta (allow), use att before the next verb: vi tillät dem att gå = we allowed them to go.
Lämna means leave, but lämna in means hand in or submit. The particle in changes the meaning: lämna in rapporten.
Tänka takes på for what you think about: tänka på saken = think about the matter. Not tänka saken.
Ta det lugnt is the set phrase for take it easy or relax. Lugnt keeps its neuter -t here.
